business_reasoning: Business-value evidence is what makes a lead worth working; it is the majority of the score so that a durable commercial signal outranks a transient clock.
Operational urgency is a real but secondary claim on attention: it reorders work within a day, it does not redefine which leads matter.
Channel is the strongest declared intake signal in the hypothetical process and also drives the assignment SLA.
Explicit stated product interest is declared intent; weighted below channel because it is self-reported and often absent.
Validated employee band is the most reliable proxy for business-banking need and is present for almost every prospect.
Industry sets specialist coverage intent but is a coarse signal at the sector level.

External market context is contextual public-data evidence about a geography, not about the lead. Capped at 0.12 of the business-value pillar (0.078 of the total score) so geography can never dominate.
Completeness determines whether an RM can act immediately; it is an operational quality of the record rather than a measure of commercial value.
Elapsed waiting time is the most interpretable urgency signal and is always computable.
The intake and assignment clocks are the committed service promise for unassigned work; they carry the heaviest urgency weight.
Ownership clocks matter for reassignment and override decisions but do not exist for most initial routing decisions.
Work already invested raises the cost of losing the lead; it applies only where pre-decision activity exists.
